record.original_question: Does there exist a countable discrete group G such that L(G) is an existentially closed II_1 factor? And does there exist an existentially closed II_1 factor that is not isomorphic to any group von Neumann algebra?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Does there exist a countable group G such that L(G) is an existentially closed II1 factor? Does there exist an existentially closed II1 factor which is not isomorphic to a group von Neumann algebra?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A II_1 factor is an infinite-dimensional von Neumann algebra M with trivial center and a (necessarily unique) faithful normal tracial state τ : M → ℂ. For any free ultrafilter ω on ℕ, the tracial ultrapower M^ω is again a II_1 factor, with M canonically embedded as a subalgebra. Working in the continuous model theory of tracial von Neumann algebras, a II_1 factor M is called existentially closed (e.c.) if for every II_1 factor N containing M (as a unital trace-preserving subalgebra) there exists an embedding N ↪ M^ω whose restriction to M is the diagonal embedding.

For a countable discrete group G, the group von Neumann algebra L(G) is the weak-operator closure of the left regular representation of ℂ[G] on ℓ^2(G); it is a II_1 factor precisely when G has the infinite conjugacy class (icc) property.

Questions.
(a) Does there exist a countable discrete group G such that L(G) is an existentially closed II_1 factor?
(b) Does there exist an existentially closed II_1 factor that is not isomorphic to L(G) for any countable discrete group G?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in current literature on existentially closed II_1 factors. Standard references on e.c. II_1 factors (Farah–Goldbring–Hart–Sherman and follow-ups) discuss many properties such e.c. factors must satisfy (e.g., every automorphism is approximately inner; bimodule structure is restricted), but no construction of an e.c. II_1 factor of the form L(G) for a countable group G, nor a proof of nonexistence, has been published, and the question of whether all e.c. II_1 factors arise from groups remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Existentially closed II_1 factors
status_evidence.snippet: A separable II_1 factor is existentially closed if any larger II_1 factor can be realized as an intermediate subfactor of the inclusion into one of its ultrapowers.
status_evidence.claim: Defines e.c. II_1 factors and studies their properties; the question whether any L(G) is e.c. is not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: Existential closedness and the structure of bimodules of II_1 factors
status_evidence.snippet: If a separable II_1 factor M is existentially closed, then every M-bimodule is weakly contained in the trivial M-bimodule.
status_evidence.claim: Recent constraints on e.c. II_1 factors but no example of the form L(G) is exhibited.
